architecture.mechanism: sulfites as dechlorinating agents to prevent biofilm formation by eliminating residual oxidants that promote microbial growth
architecture.intervention: inject sodium bisulfite or sodium metabisulfite into the feedwater upstream of the RO membranes at a concentration sufficient to neutralize residual oxidants (e.g., 1–5 ppm) while avoiding membrane degradation, combined with periodic shock dosing (e.g., 20–50 ppm) to disrupt established biofilms without chlorine
architecture.expected_effect: reduced biofilm accumulation on polyamide membranes, extended CIP intervals to ≥3 months, and normalized flux droop <5% between cleans
architecture.falsification_test: measure residual oxidant levels (e.g., ORP) in feedwater and biofilm biomass via ATP swabs before/after sulfite intervention; compare CIP frequency and flux recovery to historical data
